node-1.label: A woman in her 60s presented with a new pruritic rash

node-2.label: The rash initially developed on the patient's legs 13 days before presentation and subsequently progressed to her feet, arms, hands, and trunk; associated symptoms included a burning sensation and occasional pain.

node-3.label: Physical examination showed numerous erythematous edematous coalescing papules and plaques on the upper and lower extremities and scattered erythematous papules and plaques on the back and buttocks; some plaques were annular and polycyclic in configuration with central hyperpigmentation, while the chest, abdomen, face, and oral mucosa were clear.

node-4.label: Medical history was notable for endometrial adenocarcinoma status post hysterectomy and recent postoperative radiotherapy totaling 50.4 Gy in 28 fractioned doses, completed 4 days after the onset of the rash.

node-5.label: The patient denied any new medications, exposure to chemotherapy, imaging with intravenous contrast, or recent travel; the remainder of her review of systems was unremarkable.

why.why: Expert analyses explicitly state that radiation dermatitis is less consistent given the widespread annular/polycyclic morphology and the eosinophil-rich infiltrate without vasculitis; the biopsy also lacks leukocytoclasia/erythrocyte extravasation. Thus confidence is reduced from 0.15 to 0.10.

The patient denied new medications, chemotherapy, intravenous contrast, and travel, and both expert analyses state drug/contact hypersensitivity is not supported by the morphology or exposure history. Confidence is reduced from 0.10 to 0.05.

Both expert analyses independently conclude that the biopsy finding of perivascular/interstitial mononuclear infiltrate with numerous eosinophils and no vasculitis, combined with the new pruritic annular/polycyclic rash and endometrial adenocarcinoma, supports an immune-mediated paraneoplastic/autoimmune process. The absence of new medications, contrast exposure, or travel further supports this over drug/contact hypersensitivity. Confidence is increased from 0.72 to 0.75, but direct immunofluorescence and serum autoimmune/paraneoplastic antibody testing were not obtained, so full confirmation remains limited.

node-9.label: Skin biopsy shows perivascular and interstitial mononuclear infiltrate with numerous eosinophils and no leukocytoclasia or erythrocyte extravasation

node-10.label: Paraneoplastic eosinophilic dermatosis associated with endometrial adenocarcinoma

why.why: The Laboratory Physician and Pathologist both identify paraneoplastic eosinophilic dermatosis as the most specific fit for the endometrial adenocarcinoma history, widespread annular/polycyclic rash, and eosinophil-rich infiltrate without vasculitis. This specificity is endorsed by the current belief, so confidence is increased from 0.65 to 0.70; however, absent direct immunofluorescence and serum autoimmune/paraneoplastic antibody panels prevent definitive confirmation.

node-11.label: Direct immunofluorescence and serum autoimmune/paraneoplastic antibody testing were not obtained
